# DM11 COACHWORK Mark I

Keep the record of a private vehicle collection on your own machine. It answers from records only, says what is missing, and never sends anything out.

## What it does (only what is backed by an implementation and a test)

- Track where each vehicle is, across several locations (home garage, storage facility, workshop, dealer, track).
- Produce a per-vehicle dossier (identity, ownership, maintenance, documents, provenance, valuation) redacted per reader.
- Keep documents with issue and expiry dates, and say which are missing rather than assuming none exist.
- Record maintenance with rules, and report what is overdue, due soon, or cannot be judged.
- Track parts, stock and fitment, and refuse to recommend a part whose compatibility is unknown.
- Total recorded spend per vehicle and per category, keeping unconverted currencies out of the total instead of counting them as zero.
- Record valuations with the basis they came from (owner statement / appraisal / market reference) and never estimate a value.
- Turn a request such as 'ready for Saturday' into a checklist and the blockers, without performing any physical work.
- Track competition events for a vehicle (when, where, which class).
- Produce the pre-event checklist and what is blocking it.
- Separate what an owner, collection manager, technician, operator and viewer can each see.
- Enforce a per-edition vehicle limit.
- Offer a documented, versioned interface that other software on the same machine can call: declared commands in, JSON out, with the returned shape checked against the declaration by actually running each command. There is no network listener and no remote access.
- Let the customer define their own report shape.
- Cover more vehicles with a one-time licence file: it never expires, and it is never checked over a network, so a purchase cannot stop working later. The product states plainly that the licence is a record of a purchase, not a lock — it is not tamper-evident.
- Answer in English, not only Japanese.

## What it does not do

- Deciding anything on the owner's behalf; valuing or appraising an asset; predicting future value or market movement; giving legal, tax, medical or investment advice; certifying roadworthiness or compliance; contacting anyone; booking, buying or paying.

## Known limitations

- It answers only the 17 kinds of question listed below. Anything else is answered with "I do not know" rather than mapped to the nearest one.
- It reports what is on record. Absence of a record is reported as unknown, never as zero or none.
- It does not judge the physical condition of anything. States it reports are derived from records.
- It cannot answer a question whose subject it cannot identify uniquely; it asks instead.
- 3 of 107 evaluation cases are answered with "I do not know" although a correct answer exists (see false_abstain). These are known gaps, not errors of fact.
- How many vehicles this build has been measured with: not measured. The scale benchmark has not been run for this build (benchmarks/scale_benchmark.py writes proof/performance.json; proof/ is not in version control). scale_measurement.json is not in this copy. Nothing here should be read as a promise about speed at any number of vehicles.
- Some operator screens are outside the message catalogue and are shown in English regardless of the chosen language (DE: 6, ES: 6, FR: 6, ID: 6, IT: 6, KO: 6, NL: 6, PL: 6, PT: 6, RU: 6, TR: 6, VI: 6, ZH: 6). They are not included in the percentages above.
- Languages other than English (JA, DE, ZH, KO, ES, FR, PT, IT, NL, PL, RU, TR, ID, VI) are machine-translated by the vendor and have not been reviewed by a native speaker.

## Not measured

These are not claims of safety. They are things this build has not measured.

- Behaviour on utterances outside the evaluation set. The set was written by the vendor and is not a sample of real customer questions.
- The margin threshold (MIN_MARGIN) is not measured: the evaluation set contains no case whose correct outcome is 'ask which of two meanings was meant'.
- Accuracy of the underlying records. The assistant reports what was entered; it does not verify it.
- Whether this product is an 'AI system' under any particular law, and whether any risk classification applies. That is a legal determination and is not made here.
- Third-party security certification (SOC 2, ISO/IEC 27001, ISO/IEC 42001): none held.
- Whether audio synthesised by this product must be marked as machine-generated, and whether a listener must be told separately from the text disclosure. Both are legal determinations and are not made here (see voice/open_questions.py). The product adds no marking today; that is a description of the build, not an answer.
- Service levels, support response times, and incident procedures: none defined.
- Translation quality. The percentages below count filled message keys, not whether the wording reads correctly. No language has been reviewed by a native speaker.

## US motor-carrier edition (49 CFR 396) — coming

**Coming: this edition is not sold and cannot be downloaded yet.** It is a separate program from the one above (its own `dm11-steward.exe`, in its own zip) and keeps its own records. The text in this section is its design draft; it will be replaced by the edition's own text when the edition is released.

For the office of a small interstate motor carrier that keeps its vehicle maintenance files on paper or in a
spreadsheet. One Windows program on one PC. It keeps the records 49 CFR 396.3 and 396.21 ask a carrier to keep,
shows what is on record and what is not, and never sends anything out.

It helps you keep the records. It is not an inspection, and it does not say that a vehicle or its records
meet the rules. The qualified inspector writes the inspection report (396.21(a)).

### What it does

- **One file per vehicle (396.3(b)(1)).** Company number if the vehicle is marked with one, make, serial number
  (VIN), year, and — when the carrier does not own the vehicle — the name of the person who furnished it.
  "Not marked" and "not owned" are recorded as answers; a field nobody has answered yet is shown as
  *not recorded*, never guessed. A serial number or year is filled only while it is empty, and a serial number
  already recorded for another vehicle is refused.
- **What is due, with its date (396.3(b)(2)).** The annual inspection is due 12 months after the last one
  (396.17(c)). Your own schedule can count miles, kilometres, days, or both ("every N mi or N days, whichever
  comes first"). The program does not suggest intervals; it uses the schedule you enter.
- **The record of inspection, repairs and maintenance, with date and nature (396.3(b)(3)).**
- **Annual inspection reports (396.21).** Attach the report file to the inspection. The file shows when the
  next inspection is due and, separately, how long the report must be kept — 14 months from its date
  (396.21(b)(1)). These are two different dates and are never shown as one.
- **How long to keep (396.3(c)).** Each record: at least 1 year from its date. When a vehicle leaves your
  control: at least 6 months after that date, whichever is later. The program never deletes a record.
- **Says what is not on record, by rule section, with the command that fills it** — for example
  `[396.3(b)(1)] Serial number (VIN): not recorded. Add it: fleet set T1 --serial NUMBER`.
- **A one-page file you can open on a phone or print** (`fleet file VEHICLE --out FILE.html`): a single HTML file
  that loads nothing from the internet.
- **All vehicles at a glance** (`fleet list`): the annual inspection date and status of each vehicle, and how
  many items are not on record.
- Screens and the file in 15 languages (English is the source; the others are machine-translated and have
  not been reviewed by a native speaker).

### What it does not do

- Driver vehicle inspection reports (396.11). Those stay on paper or in a phone app.
- Tests of bus pushout windows, emergency doors and their marking lights (396.3(b)(4)).
- Inspect a vehicle, decide whether a vehicle may be used, or say that your file would satisfy an official.
- Hours of service, ELD, IFTA, fuel, dispatch, or anything connected to the vehicle itself.
- Share records between PCs over a network, or sync to a phone. There is no network listener.
- Contact anyone, order parts, or pay for anything.

Free for up to 3 vehicles, with no time limit. For more vehicles it uses the same four licence files as above (“Buy a licence”) — one licence covers either edition. On 2026-10-21 each of the four files was added with this edition's EXE (SHA-256 `bdf2c0074780a68909d6b5d095ec25a0ac37266296617926e5674909efd35bf5`) in a new, empty records folder.

### Before you start — records stay with the edition that made them

- **This edition keeps its records in its own folder** (`%LOCALAPPDATA%\DM11 COACHWORK Fleet`), apart from the general
  COACHWORK records. Records made by this edition cannot be opened by the general edition. To move records between
  PCs, make a backup and restore it with the same edition (`dm11-steward backup create`, then
  `dm11-steward backup restore FILE`).
- **It never updates the format of existing records without asking.** If you point it at records in an older format,
  every command stops and says so, and nothing is changed. `dm11-steward fleet update-records` shows what would happen;
  `dm11-steward fleet update-records --yes` takes a copy first (`…_BEFORE-UPGRADE.sqlite` in the backups folder) and then
  updates them. After the update, a build that knows only the older format can no longer open them — the copy can.
- Restoring a backup in an older format says, in the plan, that the restored records will be updated. The backup file
  itself is not changed.

### Known limitations

- The menu you get by double-clicking the program is the general vehicle-records menu; the motor-carrier file is
  reached with the `fleet` commands.
- Maintenance categories use the general vehicle-records names (for example "Tyres" in English).
- The annual inspection is counted from the inspection date. A State inspection under 396.17(f) runs from the last
  day of its month; this program uses the earlier date.
- Whether this edition has been measured with a given number of vehicles: not measured (no scale measurement is in this copy).

### If Windows shows a warning

This program is not signed by a publisher. The first time it runs, Windows may show "Windows protected your PC".

1. Before you run it, check the file. In PowerShell in the program folder, run `Get-FileHash .\dm11-steward.exe` and compare the hash with `871da4d87f83cf02bdedcffd127cd93267664bdcd0d7a265250a75efa0dadefa` (PowerShell shows it in capital letters; that is the same value).
2. If they are the same, choose "More info", then "Run anyway".

- If Smart App Control is on, Windows blocks programs that are not signed, and this program does not run. We do not ask you to turn Smart App Control off. You can find this out with the free allowance before you buy.
- Some antivirus programs may block or remove a program that is not signed. If the hash is the same, you can report it to your antivirus vendor as a false positive.
